title: Fixed Cross Carriage and Twin Roll Longarm Quilting Frame
description: One newly authored complete fixed longarm-quilting-frame appearance. Four whole grounded legs and a common open chassis carry two full long rails. A complete cross carriage rests on four lower wheels; two transverse rails carry a second whole four-wheel saddle and one continuous long-throat machine casing with an integral lower bed, raised rear column and forward overhanging head. Two separately supported full-width cloth rollers and axles flank a single continuous blank thick cloth sheet crossing the open working field and curling over both rollers. A full side handwheel, plain top spool, blank control, two forward guide grips and finite blunt needle/presser appearances belong to the one whole assembly. All geometry independently authored, not an old sewing workstation placed on a generic table or an extracted shoe-patcher head. Unlike the old fixed tabletop bed or upturned narrow horn, the broad roll-held field surrounds a two-stage rail carriage with a full long-clearance head. Four opaque PBR roles, metres Z up and whole horizontal bounds-centred ground origin; one model zero scenes. Static artistic machine exterior with one blank display cloth only: no sewing, cutting, needle motion, stitch formation, thread path, carriage travel, roller rotation, tension, workpiece compatibility, ergonomics, load, manufacture or operating safety. Rigging animation interaction not made.
